title: If you have Kenney's Asset Forge, I made a workspace/factory you can use with Claude Code to create any model you want.
author: Melodic_Charity_1770
selftext:
The workspace I built and released on github by itself is free, though [Asset Forge is a paid product by Kenney](https://kenney.itch.io/assetforge), aka the Asset Jesus. Still, the benefit is huge since it can create models much faster and much cheaper than a blender MCP setup ever will.

The result are deliberately low-poly/retro and there are around a thousand model pieces to combine in virtually infinite ways.

comments.author: Melodic_Charity_1770
comments.body:
https://i.redd.it/l1i9nxkqt60i1.png

A showcase of whats this method/workflow is capable of - you have textured or flat colors as output, plus choose to render them as crisp pixel art. The examples are crude and quick, but the potential is enormous.

comments.author: DavoDivide
comments.body: Hey so I've been making my own tools with AI and one of things I made was a low poly editor in three.js but it allows me to work on my PC, or my phone, or even in VR - one of its aspects (besides sculpting and polygon editing) is you can drag objects around and snap them to a grid. I knew about Asset Forge, I have a bit of experience with 'kit bashing' in various different software but like... is Asset Forge still relevant today? Like I thought it was old software (I mean specifically the software, all the assets and stuff are awesome)

replies.author: Melodic_Charity_1770
replies.body:
The biggest benefit that will never go stale in Asset Forge is huge library of pieces that have been hand-made. I don't remember the exact number of pieces but there's hundreds for sure, all standardized.

With 3js you still gotta spend tokens to build stuff from absolute scratch, but all those pieces in asset forge provide a big benefit.

Fun fact about the workspace I'm offering via GitHub here is that it doesn't actually even touch the asset forge exe at all - it simply extracts the pieces into a massive categorized library and provides a html form that you can fill up and paste into Claude code as a work order.

You do still get results that *can be opened and edited in asset forge* afterwards, so in that sense it still remains as a useful tweaking tool or previewer.

replies.author: DavoDivide
replies.body: Omg I thought this was a thing for making models FOR Asset Forge - but thanks for the information I figured people probably use it for the massive library compared to just kitbashing within Unity or something.

comments.author: Specialist_Aerie_175
comments.body:
This is super cool, this works for windows only

replies.author: Melodic_Charity_1770
replies.body: It works on all platforms - asset forge itself is available for Win/Mac/Linux, but this workspace repo doesn't care about platform since it simply needs the models that Asset Forge contains + it offers a HTML based requisition form that works on any browser.

replies.author: Niconame
replies.body:
I hope as more mature project are released it will help. 

And I appreciate this demo of a potential workflow, but ideally, this would be something that could be presented as, take your selection/creation of assets, and combine those in more ways. 

Instead right now it comes across more as feed this into your agent, and you can make a visually identical game to mine. ¯\_(ツ)_/¯

Maybe if you could present some very different looks achieved by these assets packs as examples that could help though.

replies.author: Melodic_Charity_1770
replies.body:
Oh you meant it that way; a concern of "if others use it, it will result in identical styles, therefore asset-flip".

I'm far too busy to build actual examples but it's not an issue at all - the models can take in textures, a shader can change how they appear in a game, lighting/compositing can be done, and the models themselves can be guided/assembled in endless ways - to emphasize height, spiky part usage, or whatever other gimmick to make these differentiate in virtually endless ways.
